operations.old: A framework-neutral `SolverTrainer` provides the first explicit training-loop boundary, and `TrainingCheckpoint` represents resumable trainer state without importing a concrete ML framework. Training checkpoints now have deterministic JSON serialization/deserialization with strict top-level field validation. The next solver step should connect `SolverTrainer` progress to `TrainingCheckpoint` creation/restoration so resumed runs preserve step semantics before any model/optimizer state is introduced. This remains solver-local, so focused validation is sufficient until a concrete trainer backend or cross-subsystem integration is added.
operations.new: A framework-neutral `SolverTrainer` provides the first explicit training-loop boundary, and `TrainingCheckpoint` represents resumable trainer state without importing a concrete ML framework. Training checkpoints have deterministic JSON serialization/deserialization with strict top-level field validation. `SolverTrainer` progress is now connected to checkpoint creation/restoration through the same explicit training-state contract, including step-consistency validation on resume. The trainer/checkpoint contracts and serialization helpers are exported through the public `poker.solver` surface so future training consumers do not depend on internal module paths. The next solver step should define the minimal framework-neutral trainable-backend contract that consumes validated solver batches and can later own model/optimizer state, without selecting Torch yet or wiring policy execution into Arena. This remains solver-local, so focused validation is sufficient until a concrete backend or cross-subsystem integration is added.
